finding.summary: An old canceled read's finalizer compared caller IDs only. After retention eviction and ID reuse, it could clear the newer turn's admission/dispatch state, allowing concurrent admission or losing cancellation ownership.

fix: Bridge active/dispatching execution references now store the exact AgentTurn object. Admission, interruption and finalization use that identity, independently of the caller-ID-keyed retained-turn map. Public turn IDs, replay and bounded retention semantics are unchanged.

regression.cases: Four deterministic cases: old canceled transcript read resolves/rejects after eviction and ID reuse, while the new instance is preparing/dispatched. Each checks busy rejection for another turn, legacy send and managed stop; cancellation must succeed, and dispatched work must still invoke the native interrupt.
regression.beforeFix: All four cases failed against a37ba84: preparing cases admitted another turn (202 versus required 409), and dispatched cases could not settle the new instance as interrupted.
regression.afterFix: All four pass; the old canceled instance never dispatches. Existing transcript/image-capability cancellation tests remain passing.
